title: Verifier‑Augmented Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) to Prevent Unsafe Network Configurations — Preregistered Reparations
research_question: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven generate–verify–repair loop reduce the rate of safety‑violating network configurations compared to LLM-only generation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: An LLM+verifier GVR loop produces a lower proportion of configurations that violate the preregistered safety property set than LLM-only single‑pass generation (paired comparison).
H0: There is no difference in the proportion of safety violations between LLM+verifier GVR and LLM-only generation.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: What is the distribution of repair iterations required before the verifier accepts a configuration?
EQ2: What failure modes remain (verifier false negatives, unresolved repairs, verifier-induced brittle repairs)?
EQ3: How do different verifier property‑sets (strict vs. permissive) change the tradeoff between safety violations and successful repair convergence?
benchmark_scope: Intent-to-configuration tasks derived from public NetOps task templates and configuration snippets (public datasets and templates only).
Safety properties defined over reachability, ACL semantics, and default-route constraints as implemented in the chosen verifier(s).
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API endpoint for all generation and repair calls (exact endpoint identifier and version will be recorded in the execution manifest).
transformation_scope: AST normalization and canonicalization of generated configurations.
Placeholder/token substitution and deterministic rendering prior to verifier invocation.
Semantic-equivalence checks (normalized-AST and simple forwarding/ACL simulation) before and after repairs.
primary_estimand: Paired difference in safety‑violation rate: proportion of tasks with final configurations violating the preregistered safety property set under LLM-only generation minus that under LLM+verifier GVR.
secondary_estimands: Absolute and relative reduction in violation rate (percentage points and percent change).
Distribution (mean, median, IQR) of repair iterations to first verifier pass.
Proportion of tasks where GVR fails to reach a verifier‑passing config within max iterations.
sampling_plan: Paired-task design. Recommended scenario: N=400 independent intent-to-configuration tasks sampled deterministically from public NetOps templates and synthetic variations (100 per difficulty cluster: simple ACL/routing change, moderate translation, multi-device change, multi-policy constraints). Inclusion: tasks mappable to a single configuration fragment. Exclusion: tasks requiring vendor‑private/proprietary features. Pairs: for each task, generate (a) LLM-only single-pass config and (b) GVR loop starting from same intent; record outcomes for both.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary confirmatory test: McNemar's test for paired binary outcomes, two-sided α=0.05. Target detectable absolute reduction ≈10 percentage points (e.g., from 20% to 10% violations). Power calculations documented in execution manifest; with N=400 estimated power ≈0.85–0.95 under assumed discordant pair split. Sensitivity analyses will recompute power for baseline violation rates 15% and 25% and alternative discordant splits. Report paired absolute difference and 95% CI (Agresti‑Coull) and bootstrap CIs for iteration distributions.
exclusion_rules: Pairs with any technical failure (API outage, verifier crash, runtime error) will be excluded from the primary McNemar analysis and listed in an exclusion table with reasons.
Tasks requiring vendor‑private features or proprietary data are excluded prior to execution.
If deterministic template mapping fails unit tests, affected tasks are excluded and replaced deterministically (replacement rule documented in manifest).
missingness_plan: Record full execution manifest including errors. Pairs with technical failures are excluded from primary analysis and reported. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses: (1) treat excluded pairs as violations in both arms; (2) treat excluded pairs as violations only in the LLM-only arm. No multiple imputation (human annotation not allowed). All exclusion counts and reasons reported.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: McNemar's test on paired binary outcomes (violation/no violation) with α=0.05; report p-value, paired absolute difference, 95% CI (Agresti‑Coull). Secondary analyses: compute risk difference and relative risk with CIs; bootstrap 95% CIs for repair-iteration distribution; report proportion unresolved within max iterations. Prespecified subgroup analyses by task cluster (exploratory if underpowered). All analyses reproducible and code + seeds recorded in execution manifest. Flagged/contaminated items analyzed separately and included in sensitivity bounds.
multiplicity_plan: Only one primary confirmatory test (McNemar) — no multiplicity adjustment for the primary outcome. Secondary and subgroup analyses are exploratory; report unadjusted p-values and CIs and label as exploratory.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: LLM overfitting to verifier (producing brittle syntactic fixes), verifier blind spots (false negatives), cross-task leakage via deterministic template derivation. Detection procedures: AST normalization to detect syntactic evasion; verifier unit tests with injected-bug cases to estimate false negatives; random 5% automated audit re-checking accepted configs under a stricter property set and alternate verifier script. Item-flagging rules: (1) flag configs that pass verifier but fail AST/semantic checks; (2) flag tasks reaching max repair iterations without verifier pass; (3) flag any technical failures. Analysis treatment: contaminated/flagged items reported separately; primary analysis excludes technical-failure pairs; sensitivity analyses treat flagged items as violations and as non-violations to bound effects. Residual uncertainty: verifier blind spots and oracle‑gaming by LLM may persist despite audits.
stopping_rule: Per-task GVR stops when the deterministic verifier accepts the config or when max repair iterations reached (initial generation + up to 4 repair iterations; max 5 LLM calls per GVR task). Overall experiment stops if the preallocated model-call budget for the selected scenario is exhausted; planned scenario is 'scn-recommended' with worst-case 2,400 LLM calls. All stopping events and counts are recorded in the execution manifest.
planned_outputs: Execution manifest with model endpoint, seeds, timestamps, hashes, and error logs.
Raw model outputs and verifier logs for every task and iteration.
Task corpus and deterministic template-mapping code with unit-test results.
Transformation & normalization code and unit tests.
Statistical-results file and analysis scripts to reproduce tests and CIs.
Failure-analysis record and contamination audit summary.
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement.
BibTeX bibliography and compiled PDF (≤5 pages).
Final autonomous revision log and output-hash manifest.
